title: European jazz musicians as copies of Americans
summary: Waters says jazz was created in America, so even the best Europeans are copies of an American model, with Django Reinhardt as an exception.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: PS: Two-parted question on being over in Europe. The major statements made on black American jazz artists going to Europe is that you get to avoid the racism of America, A, and B, be respected more for being an artist and not just, you know, that musician.

Yeah, that could be, that could be true. Because the art is newer in Europe than it is here. You haven't been, you haven't forget - don't forget that jazz was created in America and not in Europe. European, even the greatest European is a copy of an American, somebody, you understand what I mean?

The greatest - it's not true that some guys over there can't play fantastic. But you can't, like for an appearance, the guys who are technique and so forth - they can't, you can't say they're better than Americans. I mean, 'cause a lot of the things that the guys are doing now with ego, Art Tatum was doing years ago. You see what I'm talkin' about, Phil?
And so, I mean there's no one, in every jazz musician in Europe is a - not, I won't say every, there's always exceptions now, see.
Django Reinhardt was just what I mentioned, like [an] exception -
But as a rule most of 'em is a carbon copy of somebody -
